title: Momentum & Commitments QBR Toolkit
content:
Purpose: A lightweight, repeatable QBR kit that centers the conversation on momentum (what changed since last QBR), customer commitments (actions both sides agree to), and renewal signals. Two variations included below: Standard (1:1 account owner-led, 30–45m) and Enterprise (multi-stakeholder, 60–90m with technical annex). This doc is a working template — iterate per customer and paste slide text into the hosted slide master before the meeting.

Who this is for: CSMs running renewal-focused QBRs, AE co-pilots, Solutions Engineers prepping technical hooks, and CS leadership reviewing risk & upsell motion.

Quick notes / working constraints:
- Keep executive slide to a single page — heavy execs skip long decks.
- Use measurable statements ("Saved $X/month", "Latency down Y% on model Z").
- Always surface a single clear ask at the end (renewal, pilot signoff, capacity commit).
- Bring one "easy win" action item for the customer to show momentum.

Standard QBR Outline (30–45m):
1) Title + TL;DR (1 slide)
   - One-liner: current contractual state and requested outcome (e.g., "Enterprise renewal due 2026-08 — goal: secure 12-month renewal at current committed capacity with two pilot expansions").
   - Meeting objective: decision or next-step.
   - Speaker notes: Call out renewal date and target ask within first 2 minutes.

2) Executive Snapshot (1 slide)
   - High-level metrics: MRR impact, usage vs committed, latency SLO attainment, production error rate, major incidents last quarter.
   - Visuals: small sparkline + 3 headline bullets.

3) What changed (momentum) (2 slides)
   - Wins since last QBR: features deployed, performance improvements, integrations live, business outcomes (revenue/efficiency).
   - Blockers that were removed and residual risks.

4) Value map by persona (1–2 slides)
   - Product/Eng: SLOs, deployment cadence improvements.
   - Data/ML: embedding quality improvements, inference cost per 1k tokens.
   - Business: conversion delta, CSAT changes.

5) Renewal health and risks (1 slide)
   - Risk signals: usage drop, >30d unresolved P1/P2, competing procurement timeline, budget reorg.
   - Mitigations recommended and owner.

6) Commitment tracker (1 slide)
   - Table with commitments from both sides, owner, due date, status. (See sample table below)

7) Ask & next steps (1 slide)
   - Clear asks (renewal, extra capacity, pilot approval).
   - Decision timeline and escalation path.

8) Appendix / technical annex (if needed)
   - Deep dive on latency histograms, KV cache hit rates, model variant comparisons.

Enterprise QBR Variation (60–90m):
- Same core flow but expand: stakeholder breakout (20m), detailed TCO model review (15m), and formal renewal negotiation slide with commercial options and migration plan. Add a dedicated slide for compliance and audit status (if applicable).

Sample Commitment Tracker (paste into slide as a simple table):
| ID | Commitment | Owner (R / C) | Due | Status | Notes |
| 1 | Production rollout of v2 quantized model on staging | R: SE (Evan Park) / C: Eng (Alex Ruiz) | 2026-03-15 | In progress | Need test data, PR 342 pending |
| 2 | Identify 3 production prompts for quality monitoring | C: ML Ops (Zoe Chen) | 2026-03-01 | Done | Added to Redwood Optimize eval set |
| 3 | Decision on renewal term length | C: Finance (Maya Li) / R: AE (Liam O'Connor) | 2026-04-10 | At risk | Customer evaluating competing vendor |

Playbook snippets (CSM running the meeting):
- 0–5m: Set expectations and surface renewal date.
- 5–15m: Exec snapshot + highlight 1–2 biggest wins.
- 15–25m: Risk review and concrete mitigations.
- 25–30m: Drive to a single commitment; confirm owner and date.

Risk signal checklist (fast scan during meeting prep):
- Quarterly usage < 70% of committed capacity
- More than one Sev1/P1 in last 90 days
- Procurement contact changed or new PoC requested
- No activity in product usage for 2+ weeks pre-QBR
- Large feature requests stalled >60 days

Suggested KPIs to include per account type:
- Core: committed vs actual token usage, latency p95, error rate, cost per 1k tokens
- Growth accounts: adoption of embeddings API, number of active prompt templates, pilot conversion rate
- Enterprise: audit log coverage, SOC/ISO control checklist status, Uptime SLA breaches, deployment isolation status

One-page Executive Snapshot template (text to paste into a single slide):
- Headline: "Customer X: Renewal due 2026-08 — renewal recommendation: 12-month commit"
- Topline metrics: MRR impact: $XXk, QoQ usage trend: +8%, Avg gen latency p95: 310ms, SLO attainment: 99.6%
- 3 bullets: (1) Key win (decreased inference spend by 14%), (2) Major risk (budget reorg), (3) Ask (renewal + pilot expansion)
- Decision requested: choose option A/B by 2026-04-10

Commercial option language (examples to copy):
- Option A (Preferred): 12-month renewal at current committed capacity, 10% seat discount, 30-day pilot for embeddings expansion post-signing.
- Option B (Conservative): 6-month renewal with monthly reconciliation and fixed per-token overage price.

Visual / formatting guidance:
- Keep slides to 6–12 bullets max. No dense tables (appendix ok).
- Use green/orange/red for commit status only on 1 slide (not in appendix unless requested).
- Where possible include an annotated screenshot of the Console (route/traces) to make performance claims credible.

Meeting prep checklist for CSM (quick):
- [ ] Pull last 90 days usage from Console (link to route-level stats)
- [ ] Confirm renewal date and current legal owner (AE or procurement)
- [ ] Validate top 3 tickets in last quarter and mitigation status
- [ ] Pre-fill commitment tracker with owner suggestions
- [ ] Send pre-read to customer 48 hours before meeting (one-pager exec snapshot)

Follow-up and cadence after QBR:
- CSM to share final slide PDF + commitment tracker within 24 hours
- Weekly status thread for outstanding commitments with owner updates until all are complete or moved to backlog
- If renewal decision is delayed >14 days past target, trigger AE + CS leader sync and escalate per playbook (link in linked_artifacts)

Open questions / TODOs (for this template):
- Should we include a compact TCO microsheet per customer? (Pros: helps procurement, Cons: heavy lift for CSM)
- Standardize 3 commercial option templates for faster quoting — owner: AE ops (Liam)
- Add a one-click export from Console to pre-fill Executive Snapshot (tracked in JIRA-CS-6500)

Notes to self: keep this doc lean and adaptable. We want consistent behavioral asks across CSMs (one clear ask + 2 mitigation steps). Use this kit as the base for customer-specific decks.

Patch history: Initial draft 2025-11-04 (PM), revision with metrics checklist 2026-01-12 (LC), added enterprise annex 2026-02-28 (ZC).

End of doc.
